chunks: And by this chain of transmission, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Ali ibn Maymun al-Sa'igh, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) say:

Whoever desires that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, admit him into His mercy and settle him in His Paradise, let him beautify his character, extend fairness from himself, show mercy to the orphan, help the weak, and humble himself before Allah who created him.

key_terms.الضَّعِيفَ: the weak — those who lack strength, resources, or social standing
key_terms.النَّصَفَةَ: equity/fairness — giving others their due from oneself
key_terms.الْيَتِيمَ: the orphan — a particularly vulnerable member of society frequently mentioned in both Quran and hadith
key_terms.خُلُقَهُ: moral character, the sum of one's disposition and conduct
key_terms.يَتَوَاضَعْ: to show humility/lowliness — submission before God as the creator

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about entering God's mercy and paradise?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) teaches a comprehensive ethical framework for attaining divine mercy and paradise. The hadith identifies five virtues — good character, fairness to others, compassion for orphans, assistance to the weak, and humility before God — as pathways to God's mercy. This teaching reflects the Imam's emphasis on practical piety expressed through social responsibility and moral refinement, delivered to his companions in early Abbasid Kufa.
word_analysis: and let him show mercy to

en.bilal-muhammad: And by this isnad, from al-Hasan b. `Ali b. Abi Hamza from `Ali b. Maymun al-Sa'igh. He said: I heard Aba `Abdillah al-Sadiq (as) say:

Whoever would like Allah to bring him into His mercy and settle him in His Paradise should beautify his character, be fair in personality, be merciful to the orphan, help the weak, and humble himself before Allah who created him.
